# Project Angerona (AngeronaSuite) - llms.txt

Version: 1.12.1
Date: 2026-08-29
License: MIT
Repository: https://github.com/Ag3nt47/AngeronaSuite

## PRODUCT CONTRACT

Angerona is a local-first defensive EDR/NDR/SOAR and digital-forensics
workbench with safe ATT&CK validation and a local Ollama assistant. It is for
home labs, defensive research, learning, purple-team practice, and
security-engineering portfolios.

It is not an independently certified commercial EDR/XDR product. It does not
claim complete attack coverage, state/agency attribution, fleet parity, router
or firmware control, tamper-proof user-mode evidence, or externally validated
efficacy.

No offensive payload, exploit, credential theft, evasion, remote scan,
persistence, attack infrastructure, hack-back, log deletion, arbitrary
response shell, downloaded executable skill, unverified model, or unsigned
kernel component is a product capability.

## LATEST: v1.12.1 / Cycles 26-30

- Inventory truth: 81 Windows-target built-in capabilities, six native v12
  contracts and 75 explicit compatibility adapters. Every built-in module
  implementation label is 1.12.1; this does not turn compatibility metadata
  into native declarations or claim detection efficacy.
- SentinelLens is a bounded in-memory threat-hunting graph over explicit
  Syslog, Windows Event JSON/JSONL, NetFlow JSON/JSONL, and live EventBus
  evidence. An app-owned background service performs bounded non-blocking
  ingestion, reports queue/parser/analysis loss, and maintains deterministic
  snapshots without delaying sensors. It shows anomaly reasons, exact node
  evidence, and proposal-only remediation. Optional model explanation is
  restricted to a strict loopback endpoint; no cloud fallback or public/LAN
  listening socket is created.
- Guided Auto Adapt combines security-intent choices, complete-evidence gates,
  immutable exact planning, no-write simulation, recovery-baseline custody,
  and separate final approval. The recovery baseline covers complete Windows
  Firewall policy only, not the whole host.
- Every sub-100 module state requires a bounded reason. When provenance is
  provable, Capability Center/Module Inspector show a governed repository path,
  SHA-256 source identity, exact line, public source link, and red read-only line
  highlight. A missing field anchors explicitly to its owning class declaration;
  unavailable or untrusted runtime source is disclosed instead of guessed.
  Unknown, stale, lossy, unsupported, or untrusted evidence cannot be complete.
- Five three-round defensive loops (26-30) reviewed all built-in module files,
  compared primary-source upstream projects, added per-module gates, and used
  repeated independent hostile re-attacks. Tests are inert and temporary; no
  live exploitation, credential collection, persistence, hack-back, or remote
  target scanning is performed.
- Red Team Simulation binds the complete mandatory plan/denominator, exact
  process and detector generations, object custody, native receipts, and the
  signed AAR display/action handoff. The GUI defaults to 38 mandatory stages and
  37 simulation-validation contracts, including 24 fixed inert marker probes;
  native analytic catches remain separately reported. It is not a penetration-
  testing engine and executes none of the named ATT&CK behaviors.
- GitHub CI and Security assurance workflows are required post-publication
  gates. The prior Windows CI failure was isolated to CRLF conversion of a
  byte-canonical fixture and an incomplete symlink-test trust pin; the fixes
  preserve strict production validation. Final-SHA workflow status is verified
  on GitHub rather than inferred from local tests.
- Terminal release evidence on the exact v1.12.1 tree:
  2665 passed / 13 intentional host-platform
  skips / 0 failed; `compileall`, Ruff, selfcheck 26/26, workflow-policy,
  dependency-audit, documentation-drift, and diff gates passed. The guarded
  publisher verified release commit
  `0906e5bf8598379a7e7ed1477c180378c41d8e73` on canonical public `main` and
  proved all 4/4 README images byte-identical to the checked-out files.
- Detailed evidence: `analysis/loop/cycles26-30-summary.md` and
  `analysis/loop/cycle26/` through `analysis/loop/cycle30/`.

## PRIOR: v1.12.0 / Cycle 25

### Capability and version truth

- The reproducible Windows-target inventory contains exactly 80 capabilities.
  Every capability receives a validated
  `angerona.capability-contract.v12` contract and common operational
  lifecycle/freshness/loss snapshot.
- Contract maturity is explicit: 5 native contracts and 75 compatibility
  adapters. Implementation versions are 51 at 1.0.0, 28 at 1.1.0, and one
  macOS Observe preview at 0.1.0. Product semver and capability implementation
  semver are independent; never call all 80 native v12 implementations.
- Capability Center and Module Inspector search, filter, typed-sort, and open
  bounded details for contracts, source, dependency, permission, path,
  lifecycle, freshness, loss, and recent evidence.

### Guided Auto Adapt and firewall recovery

- Guided Auto Adapt presents closed Balanced, Public, and Emergency Lockdown
  choices. It performs audit, completeness gating, immutable planning, and
  no-write simulation. Accepted choices are copied immutably before background
  work; an optional apply needs a separate confirmation of the exact plan.
- Context automation is proposal-only. Legacy/tampered `auto_apply` state is
  reset false; AI/content/observations do not authorize unattended mutation.
- Recovery baseline enrollment is explicit, HMAC-authenticated, host-bound,
  and non-replaceable. Apply refuses before mutation without a complete
  baseline. The baseline restores complete Windows Firewall policy only—the
  complete mutation scope of Host Adaptation—not hardware, services, ports,
  applications, network devices, or whole-host configuration.
- Every apply has a pre-change snapshot, HMAC transaction journal, exact
  verification, compensation, startup reconciliation, and circuit breaker.
  Fresh bounded WTS, SSH/current-session, and common remote-control agent
  process checks reduce lockout risk; unknown evidence cannot authorize.
- Run safe automatic checkup audits once and simulates all profiles without
  writing.

### Clickable evidence and bounded work

- Shared tables sort typed severity and numeric risk rather than display text.
  Adaptation, alert, Live Defense, Context Info, CVE, capability, module, and
  governed-path rows open bounded read-only details.
- Alert identity, deterministic fingerprint, and verified HMAC authenticity
  are distinct labels. Analysis is bounded to 2 active workers plus 6 queued
  exact event identities with deduplication.
- Exact-rule suppression is confirmed, 15-minute, audited, undoable, and never
  available to integrity alerts. SOAR clear creates an atomic recoverable
  archive/digest manifest and restore refuses overwrite. CVE workers are owned
  and nonblocking.

### Durability, authority, and hardening

- SIEM/Remote use bounded durable outboxes, monotonic revision cursors,
  drain-stage-drain, explicit gap receipts, leases/retry/dead-letter,
  persistent tombstones, and HMAC-authenticated mutable state. The local queue
  key is independent of transport-key rotation.
- Delivery is at least once and may duplicate. Row deletion/whole-database
  rollback is not independently witnessed. Transport-key coordination uses
  restart epochs.
- Settings and Intel Sync use atomic publication; Settings compensates exact
  settings bytes, protected credentials, environment projection, and autostart.
- Evolution, mitigation tuning, contextual adaptation, and unapproved
  behavioral learning are proposal-only. Behavioral activation requires exact
  SHA-256 approval and hash drift returns to pending review.
- Self-integrity covers full callable semantics. Persistence uses explicit
  COMPLETE/PARTIAL/UNKNOWN. Process/driver/direction-specific firewall actions
  bind exact identities, return codes, postconditions, and rollback. Ambiguous
  ACL lockdown is not a production automatic action.
- IPC key custody uses the OS protected store with exact legacy plaintext
  migration/residue removal. IPC Guard is an authenticated loopback diagnostic
  admission preview, not a production payload consumer or TPM-backed channel.

### Standards and upstream comparison

- ATT&CK 19.2 curated endpoint catalog across 15 Enterprise tactics;
  Navigator 5.3.2/layer 4.5; constrained-preview OCSF 1.8 typed resolving
  observables; deliberately limited Sigma subset with atomic bounded
  admission/refusal receipts. These are not complete ATT&CK coverage, OCSF
  compiler, or full Sigma compatibility claims.
- Primary-source comparison used Velociraptor client monitoring/local buffers,
  Wazuh stateful/stateless Active Response, Fleet policy definitions, osquery
  packs/selectors, Elastic detection-as-code validation, and Velociraptor
  community-artifact warnings. Angerona adapted local design lessons; it does
  not claim their fleet/server/content ecosystems or support model.

### Performance and verification

- Recorder handoff: 22.306 -> 15.925 us/event (28.6% faster).
- Capability summary: 43.324 -> 1.508 us/call (96.5% faster).
- Stable Module Inspector tick: 13.458 -> 0.474 ms (96.5% faster).
- Batched durable commits, immutable compiled Sigma plans, and a global per-CVE
  detail-worker cap are proposed, not shipped.
- Authoritative serial release evidence, including the 3 final-performance
  tests: 1,811 passed / 6 expected host-platform skips / 0 failed. The added
  tests and their surrounding performance/reliability group also passed a
  focused 106/106 gate.
- Compile 346/346; 82/82 module files imported; 64/64 compatibility hooks;
  80 capability discovery; 92 core/module self-tests passed plus EventBus and
  12 expected inactive/platform skips; selfcheck 26/26 direct and batch; Ruff
  and diff checks clean.
- Full disposition, upstream sources, tests, and residuals:
  `analysis/loop/cycle25/summary.md`.

## LATEST: v1.11.0 / Cycle 24

### Module and platform facts

- Static platform discovery: 80 Windows modules, 14 Linux modules, 13 macOS
  modules.
- Windows contract: Protect in elevated user mode; no unsigned kernel driver.
- Linux contract: Observe plus optional privileged BCC/eBPF supplement. This is
  not a universally shipped CO-RE kernel sensor.
- macOS contract: Observe preview; no Endpoint Security or Network Extension
  enforcement claim.
- Final converged serial validation: 1,675 collected across 229 files; 1,670
  passed; 5 expected host-capability skips; 0 failed.

### Authenticated evidence and advanced correlation

- `core/sensor_provenance.py` provides strict, bounded,
  producer-authenticated event envelopes with exact schemas, sequence/replay
  state, loss metadata, and consumer constraints. EventBus HMAC protects stored
  bytes; it does not prove in-process producer identity.
- `modules/ssh_surface_guard.py` (SSHG) is observe-only. It inventories
  bounded OpenSSH configuration/Include graphs, configured public-key/CA/
  principals sources, public-key fingerprints and custody, services, listeners,
  fixed-provider authentication evidence, and normalized forwarding.
- SSH live ingestion requires the broker-assigned producer
  `OpenSSH Auth Event Collector`, exact event type, fixed provider/channel/
  message schema, and loss-aware sequence continuity. Rejected consumer schema
  does not consume continuity invisibly.
- SSHG never reads a private key or credential, attempts login, probes a
  listener, opens a tunnel, changes configuration, or retains/publishes full
  commands, full command lines, or raw endpoints.
- `modules/audit_log_guard.py` (ALIG) detects observed clear/tamper identities,
  audit-policy/logging-service changes, continuity/generation gaps, record
  reuse, provider/channel rejection, and authenticated cursor damage. It never
  clears, alters, restores, or reconstructs a Windows log.
- `modules/temporal_tradecraft_correlator.py` (TTCR) performs bounded,
  restart-aware ordered correlation for SSH persistence/session/tunnel,
  network-path drift, and log-clear sequences.
- `modules/identity_session_guard.py` (IDSG) consumes authenticated structured
  identity/session evidence for privacy-tokenized LUID/session, device-code,
  new-device, browser-store, RMM, and privilege-transition analytics. It does
  not acquire credentials, tokens, browser contents, or tenant sessions.

### Platform, driver, peripheral, and recovery posture

- `modules/driver_provenance_guard.py` (DPVG) joins image SHA-256,
  Authenticode/catalog evidence, blocklist disposition, Hypervisor-Protected
  Code Integrity, and Secure Boot. It is read-only; overflow and unknown
  evidence are explicit. On-disk evidence is not claimed as perfect loaded-
  kernel-image identity.
- `modules/platform_attestation_guard.py` (PATG) observes local Secure Boot,
  virtualization-based security, HVCI, boot flags, and TPM presence. Hardware
  attestation is reported only when an injected verifier accepts a fresh
  nonce-bound quote. The default collector does not fabricate one.
- `modules/peripheral_dma_guard.py` (PDMG) observes Kernel DMA/IOMMU,
  Thunderbolt, USB4, removable-storage, and device-install posture. It does not
  control devices or prove device firmware. Linux removable absence is complete
  only when every enumerated flag is a stable no-follow valid zero.
- `modules/immutable_recovery_guard.py` (IRAG) evaluates externally signed
  recovery-copy evidence. Quorums are satisfied inside one exact expected
  revision/archive/manifest cohort; restore tests bind to that cohort.
  Excessive future timestamps, mixed cohorts, unstable/linked evidence, and
  unbounded directories fail closed. No restore is performed.

### Network zero trust and Personal Sentinel

- `modules/network_trust_monitor.py` (NZTR) treats every active physical
  Wi-Fi/Ethernet path as untrusted. Restart-safe privacy tokens represent DNS,
  DHCP, route, gateway, profile, interface generation, and path additions.
- `core/personal_sentinel_gateway.py` is the explicitly enrolled direct-HTTPS
  first-hop client. It requires normal TLS/hostname validation plus a leaf
  certificate pin, nonce/freshness, expected policy digest, optional mTLS,
  complete IPv4/IPv6 selected-route evidence, no proxy/redirect, and unchanged
  pre/post route context.
- `core/personal_sentinel_authority.py` and
  `tools/personal_sentinel_server.py` supply a separately operated reference
  authority/server for mandatory production mTLS, Ed25519 response/state
  signing, trusted-time receipts, and monotonic compare-and-swap evidence.
  Admission is bounded; the state has singleton custody, durable sequence
  floors, and irreversible close semantics.
- Intended topology: Angerona host -> operator-controlled Personal Sentinel
  gateway/firewall -> upstream/ISP router -> Internet.
- Sentinel is not a bundled router/appliance, routing role, management plane,
  remote command service, or firmware attestor. It performs no router
  discovery/configuration, credential storage, route change, firewall mutation,
  or firmware trust. A positive first-hop label grants no endpoint, identity,
  application, destination, or upstream-router trust.
- Operators must independently provision the reference service host,
  certificates, key custody, protected state, enrollment, monitoring, backup,
  and recovery. Local signed/ACL-protected floors do not resist privileged
  whole-host snapshot rollback without a TPM or independent witness.
- `core/process_egress_lease.py` is a process/start/user/destination/path/
  budget policy broker; `modules/process_egress_guard.py` (PELG) observes its
  authenticated audit stream. It is not a firewall. Enforcement requires a
  separately privileged injected adapter and retained OS process/file identity.

### Release trust

- Public Windows first install: signed full-trust x64 MSIX only. Windows must
  validate the MSIX block map and exact provisioned publisher identity before
  activation.
- The release workflow requires an externally configured package name,
  publisher distinguished name, publisher certificate, and protected signing
  environments. The repository does not claim Microsoft Store deployment.
  Enterprise/App Installer policy and clean-VM validation are external gates.
- Classic Inno Setup is non-public, restricted, and prior-approved-install
  migration-only. It performs unelevated preflight and delegates UAC/mutation
  to the protected installed updater. It is not a public release asset or
  first-install bootstrap.
- Portable ZIP install is upgrade-only. The installed native verifier checks
  the exact candidate, payload manifest/catalog, SBOM/provenance digests,
  threshold authorization, enrolled roots, protected ACL custody, and numeric
  release version/sequence floor before target mutation.
- Signer jobs have separate protected environments. A signer response contains
  only signer ID, statement digest, and signature. The finalizer requires the
  exact separately supplied canonical 2-of-2 root policy and protected policy
  SHA-256. Signer artifacts cannot replace authority roots.
- A local protected rollback floor cannot resist privileged restoration of the
  whole host. TPM-backed or independently witnessed monotonic state is needed
  for that attacker model.
- `modules/release_transparency_guard.py` (RTAG) is runtime observe-only
  defense in depth. It is not the first-install trust bootstrap.

### ARIA Defense Memory and RAG provenance

- `assets/angerona_defense_memory.json` is Defense Memory v1.1.0 with 18
  capability, usage, defensive-measure, limit, and actor-neutral tradecraft
  entries.
- `core/defense_memory.py` admits it only after stable non-reparse bounded
  reading, strict duplicate-free schema validation, structural/text limits, and
  canonical digest verification:
  sha256:97a7771a9ce38ac66c6889dc90e0d591b64e07c2f169a0cebd7a57c119d67d57
- Defense Memory is data-only. It defines no tool, action, prompt authority, or
  executable procedure. Local retrieval can use its admitted content. If a
  cloud fallback is separately enabled and authorized, at most one
  highest-ranked canonical Defense Memory excerpt is redacted and eligible.
- `modules/rag_provenance_guard.py` (RAGP) validates explicitly configured,
  root-confined, digest-bound future sources and emits inert taint/trust labels.
  It does not change an index or Defense Memory and needs a caller-owned
  verifier for signed trust tiers.
- Local Ollama remains the default. Model output and retrieved text are
  advisory evidence; they cannot self-authorize a tool or arbitrary PowerShell.

### Live Defense Activity

- `gui/live_defense_activity.py` requests at most 16 recent public EventBus
  records, displays at most five sanitized summaries, and adds coarse module
  health.
- It never reads event details, raw telemetry, source code, executing source,
  hidden AI reasoning, private chain-of-thought, credentials, local paths,
  addresses, SSIDs, or interface identities.
- It is an operational activity surface, not a debugger or reasoning viewer.

## RESPONSE AUTHORITY

Adversary Combat is the governed mutation boundary. Supported exact-target
classes include block exact remote peer, isolate exact executable, suspend or
terminate verified process, quarantine exact file, activate bounded deception,
explicitly isolate host, and undo verified reversible actions.

Contracts bind action, process birth, executable/file identity, peer, lifetime,
sequence, and escalation. Capability state uses durable epoch/high-water
continuity. Durable intents, verified postconditions, signed receipts, exact
Undo, startup recovery, compensation, and mutation circuit breakers make
effects visible and recoverable.

Protected/system targets, stale process identities, path replacement, ambiguous
PowerShell semantics, weak cross-entity correlation, and unsigned or malformed
authority fail closed. Model output, retrieved content, public EventBus text,
and observe-only module findings never grant response authority by themselves.

## ARCHITECTURE

- `src/angerona/core/`: EventBus, provenance, policy, response contracts,
  capability authority, file/process leases, trusted time, Sentinel authority,
  recovery, release authority, ARIA/RAG, evidence, cases, custody, and platform
  abstractions.
- `src/angerona/modules/`: independent BaseModule detectors/responders.
- `src/angerona/gui/`: dashboard, Live Defense Activity, Flow Dashboard /
  Local SOC, operations, Settings, Scan Center, Red Team, ATT&CK, Combat
  history/Undo, ARIA, and Upgrade Console.
- `src/angerona/shark/`: bounded non-destructive simulations and AAR evidence.
- `src/angerona/telemetry/`: bounded process/network snapshots and normalized
  sensor data.
- `tools/`: compile/selfcheck/release/validation helpers and Personal Sentinel
  reference server.
- `analysis/loop/`: red-team, remediation, performance, innovation, and
  verification evidence.

Normal flow:

sensor -> broker-authenticated typed evidence -> HMAC EventBus -> recorder /
correlation -> incident / SOAR -> signed response contract -> Adversary Combat
-> durable intent -> exact action -> verified postcondition -> signed receipt
-> Undo / recovery

## DATA, SECRETS, AND EGRESS

- Source/development data uses the checkout sibling `AngeronaData`.
- Packaged Windows data prefers protected `D:\AngeronaData`, with protected
  `%ProgramData%\Angerona` fallback.
- macOS uses its application-support area; Linux uses XDG state.
- Secrets use Windows DPAPI, macOS Keychain, or Linux Secret Service when the
  protected backend is required.
- Runtime data, credentials, private signing material, diagnostics, journals,
  models, evidence, and local state are not source artifacts and must not be
  committed.
- Cloud, messaging, SIEM, threat-intelligence, and peer integrations are
  optional and off by default. Any selected data crossing an enabled connector
  remains subject to its separate consent/redaction contract.

## BUILD, RUN, AND VALIDATION

Windows source:

    Install-Angerona.bat
    start-angerona.bat

Development:

    python -m pip install -e ".[dev]"
    python -m pytest -q
    python -m ruff check src tests tools
    python tools/compile_check.py
    python tools/selfcheck.py
    run-selfcheck.bat
    python run_aria_selftests.py
    run-adversary-combat-validation.bat

## CYCLE 25 FINDING DISPOSITION

- Round 1 recorded 12 traceable risk/reliability lineages without invented
  retrospective CVSS scoring; all are fixed or truthfully scoped.
- Round 2 re-audited 8 overlapping durability/lifecycle records and fixed all
  8, including one IPC self-test concurrent-accounting race.
- Round 3 performed 12 final closure checks and found no open High/Critical code
  finding in the v1.12 change set.
- Accepted boundaries include firewall-only recovery scope, at-least-once
  duplicates, no independent witness for outbox deletion/whole-DB rollback,
  restart-epoch transport-key coordination, constrained OCSF/Sigma, diagnostic-
  only IPC, and 75 compatibility adapters.

See `analysis/loop/cycle25/prior_findings.md` and
`analysis/loop/cycle25/summary.md`.

## CYCLE 24 FINDING DISPOSITION

- Round 1 opened 10 defects plus 1 informational runtime/deployment boundary.
- Round 2 re-audited 7 release/integration/lifecycle issues or residuals.
- All seven Round 2 findings received code remediation and focused regressions.
- Round 3 opened 4 findings (1 High, 1 Medium, 2 Low); all four received code
  or documentation remediation and focused regressions.
- Release first-install trust still requires provisioned Windows publisher and
  deployment policy; release roots/policy still require protected external
  custody; privileged whole-host rollback still requires TPM/independent
  monotonic state.
- Broker keys, trusted-time/high-water state, recovery evidence, and Sentinel
  authority state must live outside a restorable monitored-host snapshot when
  snapshot rollback is in scope.
- Older architectural residuals remain: in-process admitted-extension authority
  (A-04), broad legacy PowerShell policy surface (A-06), and the preferred
  retained OS process/executable-file lease across path-wide firewall mutation
  (R6-03).

See `analysis/loop/cycle24/prior_findings.md` and
`analysis/loop/cycle24/summary.md`.

## PERFORMANCE EVIDENCE

- Cycle 25 recorder handoff: 22.306 to 15.925 us/event (28.6% faster).
- Cycle 25 capability summary: 43.324 to 1.508 us/call (96.5% faster).
- Cycle 25 unchanged Module Inspector tick: 13.458 to 0.474 ms (96.5%
  faster).
- Proposed only: batched durable commits, immutable compiled Sigma plans, and a
  global per-CVE detail-worker cap.
- Historical Cycle 24 evidence follows.

- Personal Sentinel canonical unsigned-state reuse: 30.2-39.0% lower measured
  serialization/signing kernel CPU across 64-4096 nonces; fsync/replace
  unchanged.
- Identity replay membership: O(n) to O(1), 410.488 us to 0.060 us at the
  artificial 4096-event bound; authoritative ordered-window semantics retained.
- Bounded directory iteration: 0.0242 ms versus 3.3220 ms in a synthetic
  100,000-row over-budget case and, more importantly, exactly limit+1 rows
  consumed.
- Fixed-schema sensor admission added 4.060 us/event in the synthetic 5,000-
  event benchmark.
- Two complete public-gallery runs produced byte-identical output.
- No optimization relaxed cadence, freshness, cryptography, stable reads,
  completeness, response authority, or fail-closed behavior.

## KNOWN LIMITS / NOT SHIPPED

- No whole-host rollback from the Host Adaptation baseline; it covers complete
  Windows Firewall policy only.
- No exactly-once exporter claim, independent outbox rollback witness, or
  coordinated no-restart transport-key epoch protocol.
- No full OCSF/Sigma implementation or complete ATT&CK coverage claim.
- No IPC production payload consumer or TPM-backed transport.
- No claim that 75 compatibility adapters are native v12 implementations.
- No turnkey Personal Sentinel appliance, router, routing role, router
  credentials, router discovery/configuration, firewall mutation, remote command
  plane, or firmware attestation.
- No automatic process-egress enforcement adapter.
- No default hardware quote provider/verifier or hardware-rooted recovery/
  release high-water.
- No authoritative cloud identity/session collector; IDSG consumes supplied
  structured evidence.
- No claim that on-disk driver bytes perfectly identify a currently loaded
  kernel image.
- No recovery from logs/evidence already deleted before collection.
- No public classic Setup first install and no Microsoft Store deployment claim.
- No independent certification, commercial fleet support, long elevated soak,
  clean-machine publisher matrix, physical sleep/resume matrix, native
  Linux/macOS release acceptance, field false-positive baseline, or independent
  efficacy evaluation.

- Cycle 25 upstream/standards sources:
  `analysis/loop/cycle25/round1/upstream_project_comparison.md`.
- CISA AA25-239A:
  https://www.cisa.gov/news-events/cybersecurity-advisories/aa25-239a

  https://www.cisa.gov/sites/default/files/2024-03/aa24-038a_csa_prc_state_sponsored_actors_compromise_us_critical_infrastructure_3.pdf

  https://csrc.nist.gov/pubs/sp/800/207/final

  https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1070/001/

  https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-server/administration/openssh/openssh-server-configuration
- Microsoft Storm-2372 device-code phishing:
  https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/security/blog/2025/02/13/storm-2372-conducts-device-code-phishing-campaign/

  https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/security/hardware-security/kernel-dma-protection-for-thunderbolt

  https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/security/operating-system-security/system-security/protect-high-value-assets-by-controlling-the-health-of-windows-10-based-devices

  https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc9334
- NIST FIPS 203 ML-KEM:
  https://csrc.nist.gov/pubs/fips/203/final

These sources support actor-neutral defensive technique selection. They do not
prove attribution, product efficacy, or completeness.
